title: What S1, the strip, waits on
ask: May S1 (strip the interior) wait only on the design rows that need the car whole, with the bench, desk and review rows gating Z1 instead?
why: S1 (strip the interior) waits today on 25 design rows, by D-387's rule that everything that can be done with the car whole is done first, so the car is off the road as short a time as possible. Only two of those rows actually need the car whole: B2 (read the wideband gauge's part number) and V-002 (read the alternator tag). The other 23 are bench, desk, KiCad, firmware and review rows (T-049 alone, a microSD card in a bench Teensy, has 61 rows waiting behind it). The measurement day C1 waits on S1, and the design review Z1 waits on C1's numbers, so today no agent design row is READY in electrical: all 14 wait, through S1, on your bench and desk rows. Two rows were gated the wrong way round (Q-028 and Q-110 needed the installed PMU yet sat in S1's and Z1's gates); they are moved to the build track. This block is about the rest.
options:
(a) Keep D-387 as it is: S1 waits on every design row that can be done with the car whole. Costs nothing now; the strip, the measurement day, the review and the freeze all wait until the bench and desk work is finished, and the interior is out only from the strip to the refit.
(b) S1 waits only on B2 and V-002; every bench, desk and review row gates Z1 (the review) instead. The measurement day can happen on your next free weekend and the design gets real numbers (R11) sooner; but under D-387 the car comes apart once, so the interior stays out while the desk work, the review, the freeze and the parts all land - weeks to months.
(c) S1 waits on B2, V-002 and the seven review rows R1-R7 (the design is reviewed before the car comes apart); the bench, firmware and KiCad rows gate Z1. The measurement day comes sooner than (a), and the review has already read the design; the interior-out time is between (a) and (b).
recommend: (a), unless you want the measurement day's numbers before the bench and desk work is finished - then (c). (b) only if you accept the interior being out for the whole procurement.
stops: Nothing stops today. It decides how soon the measurement day can come, and how long the interior is out.

title: How long the interior is out
ask: After the strip, does the car stay apart for the whole procurement and build, get refitted between the measurement day and the build, or are the long-lead parts ordered before the strip?
why: Two standing rulings meet in the work graph and nothing shows you the result. D-323: nothing is bought until the design is complete and you understand it. D-387: the car comes apart once - the strip S1, then the measurement day C1, then the review Z1 and your freeze Z2, and only then (phase SOURCING) the carts are paid (A1, A2), the parts arrive (D1), the ICU and DCU boards are laid out from the measurements (F11), ordered (F12, F5) and bench-commissioned (F3, F6), and the backbone and legs are built. Every one of those waits on the interior being out, and the interior goes back only at E35, after the harness is in. Read as a calendar: from the strip weekend, the dash and seats are out for the Deutsch shipping time, two PCB fabrications with their lead times, the bench commissioning and the build itself - weeks to months, not the "as short a time as possible" S1's own note promises, and the car is not driven meanwhile (E30). Block 01.12 asks what S1 waits on; this one asks what happens after it.
options:
(a) Keep it as it is: strip once, measure, freeze, buy, build, refit. The simplest sequence and the fewest times anything comes apart; the car is off the road for the whole procurement and build, likely months.
(b) Measure, then refit: the strip is only as deep as the measurement day needs (the cluster, the centre stack, the sill and cargo trim), the interior goes back the same weekend, and the car drives until the parts and boards are in hand; the full strip happens once more for the build. Two teardowns instead of one (D-387 is superseded on that point); the car keeps driving.
(c) Long-lead orders before the strip: the Deutsch kit, the wire and the boards' common parts are ordered from the design as it stands, before the measurement day, so the wait after the strip is only the measured cut lengths and the two boards. Money before the freeze (D-323 is amended for a named list), one teardown, a shorter time apart; the risk is a part bought wrong that a measurement would have caught.
recommend: (b), unless you can live without the car for the months between the strip and the harness going in - then (a). (c) only for parts the design cannot change (the Deutsch kit sized from the cavity tables), and named one by one.
stops: Nothing today. It decides the build sequence D-387 describes and, with (c), which parts D-323 lets through early.
